subject: Next steps: ClearEdge MAP — POC access, API keys, org setup & VPC peering
messages:
From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@clearedge.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP planning / POC access

Camila — thanks for the call today. Sara and I reviewed the MAP draft and we want to move the POC forward next week. To finalize scheduling we need a clear checklist of infra items we (ClearEdge) must complete and what Redwood will provision.

Quick questions up front:
- Will Redwood issue scoped API keys for our eval org or do we create service accounts in our cloud and exchange credentials?
- For VPC peering: do you support cross-account peering to our GCP project or should we expect a reverse peering request?
- IP allowlist: we need the exact egress IPs so our network team can open the firewall.

If you can send a minimal runbook with owners and dates that maps to the MAP milestones that'd be ideal.

Thanks,
Tom Lee
Director, Platform Ops
ClearEdge Analytics

--
Attachment: clearedge_sso_request.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@clearedge.com>, Sara Mills <sara.mills@clearedge.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP planning / POC access

Tom — great to hear. Draft MAP attached (ClearEdge_MAP_v1.xlsx) with proposed owners and a 3-week activation timeline. High level answers here and we'll fill details in the shared sheet: 

1) API keys & org setup
- Redwood will create a ClearEdge evaluation org in the console and create two scoped API keys: one for test traffic and one for metrics collection. Keys expire at the end of the POC window unless you request extension.
- If you prefer a cloud-side service account and token exchange, Karthik can run the integration flow.

2) VPC peering
- We support both peering directions. Standard approach: ClearEdge initiates peering from your project -> Redwood will accept and configure routes. If you need Redwood to initiate, we can do that with an executed network consent form.

3) IP allowlist
- We'll provide a static egress block for the POC: 34.82.110.0/24 and 35.196.200.0/24. Please confirm zone-level firewall opens for those ranges and the ports (443 outbound).

Next steps I propose:
- Karthik to run a 30-min tech runbook call (tomorrow) to walk the team through the API key flows and sample requests.
- Vivek to confirm peering window and expected CIDR translations.
- Security questionnaire & DPA: see DocuSign link in the MAP.

I'll attach the MAP and network diagram. If that sounds good I'll loop Vivek and Prioym for schedule.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: ClearEdge_MAP_v1.xlsx, poc_network_diagram.png

- Quick intro to Redwood eval org + Console access (5m)
- API key creation & scope patterns (10m)

Tom — can you paste the GCP project id you'll use for peering and the desired test CIDR? That'll let Vivek pre-check route conflicts.

Thanks,
Karthik

Thanks Karthik — we prefer Redwood-issued API keys to keep our test infra minimal. Project id is clearedge-eval-2026 and desired test CIDR for peering is 10.11.0.0/16. We've provisioned a jump-bastion in that VPC for kube access.

Also: our security team asked whether token revocation is supported mid-POC in case a key is rotated. Please confirm.

Tom

Looping in infra/security checks here — notes from my side: 
- Peering: 10.11.0.0/16 is fine. We'll request the peering from our side acceptance flow once ClearEdge shares the peering request ID. Expect maintenance window 2 hours; we'll schedule it during your non-prod hours (preferably 0200-0500 UTC).
- NAT/egress: the two /24 blocks Camila listed are the egress ranges. If you have a strict allowlist we can provide per-availability-zone IPs but that requires provisioning a small fleet in a single AZ (flag in MAP if you want that).
- Token lifecycle: Redwood admin can revoke keys immediately; we'll provide a one-click revoke button in the console UI for the scoped keys. If you request rotation we can do certificate rotation with minimal downtime (standard key swap).

I'll be available on Friday for the peering checklist and can join the call.

Vivek
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood

2) Confirm CIDR: 10.11.0.0/16 — received.
3) Confirm firewall opens for 34.82.110.0/24 and 35.196.200.0/24 outbound to 443 — please confirm.

5) SSO / admin account: we will create one Redwood eval org admin for Sara and one read-only observer for Tom; if you need SCIM provisioning supply the SCIM bearer token via the secure form.
